💬 Missing crew members found after attack on fishing boats near Iran’s Qeshm Island

📌 Qeshm, IRNA — The two fishermen reported missing after a US attack on two fishing boats off Qeshm Island have been found, the head of Qeshm’s fishing community says.

Ali Eslami Ramchahi told reporters on Saturday that the two men had been found and were returning to Qeshm.
​
He added that Mahmoud Panjeh and his son, who lost contact with shore after the attack, had been found safe and were returning. He said that Mehrzad Panjeh suffered injuries to both legs, while his brother Mehran was rescued from the sea by passing vessels.
​
Earlier, Hormozgan Province Deputy Governor Ahmad Nafisi had reported that the boats were attacked at about 11:30 a.m., 18 nautical miles from Messen village in Qeshm County.
​
Each boat carried two crew members. Two fishermen were brought to Qeshm, one injured and taken to hospital for treatment. The other two were reported missing, prompting search and rescue operations.
​
Nafisi said authorities were following up and would release details after receiving official reports.

🔊 Iran seeks joint agricultural investment with Africa: Minister

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran is seeking to expand agricultural cooperation with African countries through joint investment, technology transfer and production partnerships, Agriculture Minister Gholamreza Nouri Ghezeljeh has said.

Speaking at the first National Conference on Iran-Africa Agricultural Cooperation in Tehran on Saturday, Nouri Ghezeljeh said Iran viewed African countries as partners in production and investment rather than merely markets for its products.
​
He said Iran had expertise in irrigation, water and soil management, greenhouse production, agricultural machinery, livestock, fisheries and agro-processing that could be shared with African partners.
​
Nouri Ghezeljeh said trade between Iran and African countries reached around $940 million in the nine months starting March 20, 2025, marking a 66% year-on-year increase. However, he said, the figure remained far below the continent's economic potential.
​
He stressed the need to move beyond one-way trade toward joint investment, production, value chains and technology transfer, calling for existing agreements to be turned into practical projects and contracts.
​
The minister also announced that the fourth Iran-Africa Cooperation Summit would be held next month.
​
Addressing global food security, Nouri Ghezeljeh said US military actions had disrupted energy and food markets, with food prices rising by up to 23% in some countries, disproportionately affecting poorer communities.
​
He said Iran had maintained supplies of essential goods during the US-Israeli military aggression and called on Washington to return to the Islamabad memorandum of understanding to help end the war and ease its global economic and food-security consequences.
​
He said the success of cooperation with African countries should be measured by implemented projects and tangible economic benefits rather than the number of meetings or agreements signed.
